audit.why: FAV at 4/10 matches 55.05% over 732 games, and the page's own framing (he needs marks plus a blink, you need neither) supports it.
All seven rows read Tryndamere in both layers and every why agrees with its side, which is consistent with a 55% win rate and a lane where his kill script needs two resources.
audit.corrected: No chart change. phases[5].why re-grounded on Ashen Pursuit's flat 10s cooldown instead of an item name.

audit.whatIsWrong: Purgatory was treated purely as an execute zone. It also grounds — and grounding turns off Spinning Slash, the only mobility Tryndamere owns.
audit.why: A reader told to 'disengage above the floor or leave the totem zone entirely' will try to spin out and find the ability dead. The correct instruction is the opposite: leave before he throws it, or commit to finishing the fight inside it under Undying Rage. Real numbers: his nails are 10/9/8/7/6 at 950 range, Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s blink at 425, Soul Ignition is 18/17/16/15/14, Purgatory is 120/100/80 at 1000.
audit.corrected: Written into report[5], breakdown.cooldowns, phases[4].why, phases[5].why, spikes[1] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] said 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of its source, and Soul Ignition's whole payoff is healing back a portion of the self-damage at the end of the duration. Anti-heal is exactly the counter to that window.
audit.corrected: report[8] now ties Grievous Wounds to the end-of-duration refund.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'don't' read 'Dive him at low HP with his totem down' — backwards advice.
audit.why: A spent ultimate is when the dive is safe; the danger is diving into the zone. As written the page warns you off the good window and says nothing about the bad one.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[0].t and report[11].t now say inside his totem zone.

edits.before: Purgatory changes the rules: fights now end at HIS floor — disengage above ~15% or leave the totem zone entirely.
edits.after: Purgatory changes the rules: it grounds, so Spinning Slash cannot carry you out of the zone — leave before he throws it.

edits.before: Lich Bane spike — his blink-bite now genuinely one-shots marked squishies. Respect the all-in until his E is down.
edits.after: First-item spike — his blink-bite one-shots marked squishies. Ashen Pursuit is 10s flat, so the window after it never moves.

edits.before: Dive him at low HP with his totem down
edits.after: Dive him at low HP inside his totem zone

edits.before: Track Locke’s Ritual Nails (Marks): The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Commit only while it is down.
edits.after: Purgatory grounds you: inside its zone Spinning Slash simply does not fire, so leave before he throws it rather than after. The marks are the other half — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents at all.

edits.before: - Locke Ritual Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Track it before every step-up. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.
edits.after: - Locke's nails: 10s at rank 1, 950 range — the marks are his whole engine; without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents, so sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): a flat 10s, 425 blink and his ONLY mobility — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): 120s at rank 1, 1000 range, and it grounds — Spinning Slash will not take you out of the zone.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Grievous Wounds cuts Soul Ignition's end-of-duration refund.

edits.before: Dive him at low HP with his totem down. Eat three nail stacks before you commit. Let W’s grey health refund his mistakes — kill through the window, not around it. Don’t spend your ultimate on chip damage — it is the kill window.
edits.after: Dive him at low HP inside his totem zone. Eat three nail stacks before you commit. Let Soul Ignition's refund heal his mistakes — carry Grievous Wounds into that window. Don’t spend your ultimate on chip damage — it is the kill window.

edits.before: This is where the matchup breaks: R Purgatory is an execute, and Undying Rage makes you unexecutable for its whole duration - all-in with R up and his win condition simply does not exist.
edits.after: This is where the matchup breaks: Purgatory executes and Undying Rage covers you while it runs - but the zone grounds too, so finish the fight inside it; Spinning Slash will not carry you out.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stay yours as Fury crits stack faster than his burst windows come up. At 6 his whole win condition dies: R Purgatory is an execute and Undying Rage makes you unexecutable for five seconds, so take every all-in with your R up and simply refuse to die through his totem.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stay yours as Fury crits stack faster than his burst windows come up. At 6 his script changes: Purgatory executes and it also grounds, so Spinning Slash will not take you out of the zone — hold Undying Rage for that moment and finish the fight inside it rather than trying to walk away.

notes: Two things I did not touch and you should decide on. (1) The page calls his Q 'Ritual Nails' everywhere including focus.text and loading, but Riot's own description for that ability reads 'Locke readies a set of Soul Nails to throw'. The packet's enemyAbilities is null for Locke, so there is no authoritative name list to check against, and a half-renamed page is worse than a consistently-wrong one — I left every instance alone. (2) 'he pays for every CS at 125 range' appears in phases[0].why, breakdown.early and breakdown.wave; no attack range is published in the kit file, so I could not verify it. The kit file also tags Soul Ignition with trueDamage while Riot's text for it mentions none, so I did not assert true damage anywhere. 'resets on takedowns' for Ashen Pursuit is likewise unsupported by the text and I dropped it while rewriting breakdown.cooldowns rather than restating it.
